abstract: Efficient fine-tuning is vital for adapting large language models (LLMs) to downstream tasks. However, it requires non-trivial efforts to implement these methods on different models. We present LlamaFactory, a unified framework that integrates a suite of cutting-edge efficient training methods. It provides a solution for flexibly customizing the fine-tuning of 100+ LLMs without the need for coding through the built-in web UI LlamaBoard. We empirically validate the efficiency and effectiveness of our framework on language modeling and text generation tasks. It has been released at https://github.com/hiyouga/LLaMA-Factory and received over 25,000 stars and 3,000 forks.

sections.body: The paper states that fine-tuning large language models needs substantial resources, and that the community lacks a systematic framework that unifies efficient fine-tuning methods across models. It presents LlamaFactory, which combines efficient methods, supports pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback and direct preference optimization, and offers command-line and web interfaces. The repository is open-sourced under Apache-2.0 and has over 25,000 stars and 3,000 forks. Hundreds of models on the Hugging Face Hub were built with it.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Fine-tuning large language models is costly, so LlamaFactory unifies efficient fine-tuning methods in one framework.

sections.body: The section compares LlamaFactory with FastChat, LitGPT, LMFlow and Open-Instruct in a feature table. In that table, only LlamaFactory is marked for DoRA, LoRA+, PiSSA, BAdam, S2 attention, KTO and ORPO. The other frameworks are described as supporting chat training, instruct recipes, distributed parallelism or specialized domains. The authors state that LlamaFactory supports a broader range of efficient fine-tuning techniques and training approaches than these alternatives.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Existing fine-tuning frameworks support fewer efficient methods than LlamaFactory, as its feature comparison shows.

sections.body: The section divides efficient fine-tuning into optimization techniques, which reduce the cost of tuning parameters, and computation techniques, which reduce time or space. Optimization methods covered include freeze-tuning, GaLore, BAdam, LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA, LoRA+ and PiSSA. Computation methods include mixed precision training, activation checkpointing, flash attention, S2 attention, quantization and Unsloth. The authors state that combining these techniques reduces the memory footprint from 18 bytes per parameter during mixed precision training to 0.6 bytes per parameter. The text gives no derivation of these figures.
sections.heading: Efficient Fine-Tuning Techniques
sections.headline: The paper groups efficient fine-tuning into optimization methods, such as LoRA, and computation methods, such as flash attention.

sections.body: The section describes three modules. The Model Loader handles model initialization, patching, quantization and adapter attaching, and supports vision language models. The Data Worker covers dataset loading, aligning, merging and pre-processing into a unified format. The Trainer applies efficient methods across pre-training, instruction tuning and preference optimization. The section also introduces model-sharing RLHF, which the authors say allows RLHF training with no more than one pre-trained model, and LlamaBoard, a Gradio interface for configuring, monitoring and evaluating fine-tuning without code.
sections.heading: LlamaFactory Framework
sections.headline: LlamaFactory has three modules, Model Loader, Data Worker and Trainer, with a web interface called LlamaBoard.

sections.body: The paper evaluates training efficiency and downstream effectiveness. For efficiency, it fine-tunes Gemma-2B, Llama2-7B and Llama2-13B on a PubMed corpus of around 400K tokens and reports peak memory, throughput and perplexity on one NVIDIA A100 40GB GPU. QLoRA has the lowest memory footprint, LoRA shows higher throughput than full-tuning, and GaLore achieves lower perplexity on large models. For downstream tasks on CNN/DM, XSum and AdGen, LoRA and QLoRA achieve the best performance in most cases. Some Gemma-7B and Qwen2-7B results are omitted because GaLore may not be applicable to them.
sections.heading: Empirical Study
sections.headline: Across tested models, quantized low-rank adaptation used the least memory and low-rank adaptation scored best on most generation tasks.

sections.body: The conclusion restates that LlamaFactory uses a modular design to fine-tune over 100 LLMs with efficient techniques, and offers the web UI LlamaBoard. The authors say they will keep the framework synchronized with current models and efficient techniques. Their road map lists support for audio and video modalities, sequence and tensor parallelism, and self-play methods for conversational models. The section reports no new experiments.
sections.heading: Conclusion and Future Work
sections.headline: Future work targets more modalities, parallel training strategies and stronger methods for conversational models.

sections.body: The section says LlamaFactory has drawn many individuals exploring LLM customization and is listed in Awesome Transformers as a representative efficient fine-tuning framework. The authors expect practitioners to build LLMs on the framework in ways that benefit society. They state that adherence to the model license is mandatory when fine-tuning with LlamaFactory, which they say prevents potential misuse.
sections.heading: Broader Impact and Responsible Use
sections.headline: The authors expect the framework to benefit open-source communities, and require users to follow model licenses.
